q_a2a: Whichever stage you're at, saying the right thing when you sit down with your little one helps, but you also have to start actually doing some of it in the rest of your life. Your little one starts believing the grown-up you when they catch you lying down because you're wiped out, instead of pushing through one more chore.

q_b2a: If it's your orientation or your gender in question, I wouldn't go the other way and write it off as "just an intrusive thought" only because it's unwanted, or because your family wouldn't like it. There's no rush to decide either way, because you'll find it out over time from what you keep noticing with real people and in how you actually live, and that counts for more than any one feeling, however strong it is. Even if somebody tells you otherwise, feeling the opposite tomorrow wouldn't show you the "real you" either.
q_ka: If you're going on a date mainly to prove you're normal, or that you're really attracted to someone, you're doing the same checking you'd otherwise do in your head, just out in real life. Trying things out to find who you're attracted to is fine, though, as long as you're not testing every single moment for a final answer. A date you go on to prove something might calm you down for a day or so. Then you start going over the date itself, and the next doubt comes even bigger. If you'd want their company anyway, I'd still go, and just drop the proving part. Cancelling or leaving early just to make the doubt go away is still checking, but you can always get out if you feel unsafe, or if there's touch or sex you want to stop, and that's a different thing.
q_fa: Anxiety deserves the same kind of listening, but it isn't a fortune teller. It might really be warning you about something, like being overloaded, or a boundary. Most of the time, I'd ask it what it's trying to protect, and then check what it predicted against what actually happens, unless you're really in danger, or it's something in your body like chest pain, which a doctor should look at instead of you waiting to see if the anxiety was right. And when a part of you says no to going deeper, or to an altered state, that no isn't a prediction at all, and it's reason enough to stop. With touch or sex, even a hesitation is enough, and it might not sound like a no at all, more like a part of you going quiet or pulling back a little.
